newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices little changed in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices little changed in thin talk.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished the week little changed against Thursday's levels in thin discussion, industry sources said.
Higher crude oil and natural gas prices did provide support for domestic heavy fuel market, traders said.
Some traders said the strength in the crude prices would should have given a solid lift to resid values this week.
"It's undervalued by a dollar," said one East Coast trader.
Others argued that the lack of end-user demand and cheap natural gas prices would continue to depress resid prices.
"There's still no demand," said another East Coast trader.
In the NYH, one-percent sulphur grade was assessed at $17.00-$17.25 a barrel, flat from Thursday. Three-percent valued were unchanged from Thursday at $14.75-$15.25.
In the Gulf, prices for the one-percent grade ended at $16.00-$16.25, flat from Thursday's $16.40-$16.60 range. Three-percent values were quoted at $15.25-$15.75, unchanged from Thursday's range.
A fourth-quarter three-percent paper deal was heard done in the $15.50-$15.75 area. No physical transaction reportedly changed hands.
Meanwhile, NYMEX October Henry Hub natural gas futures settled up 5.4 cents at $1.863 per million British thermal units on firmer cash prices.
October crude oil futures ended at $23.85 a barrel, up 41 cents from Thursday's settlement due to shortcovering and a jump in heating oil prices.
New York city gate September gas prices were assessed at $2.05 today, versus NYH one percent resid at a $2.71/mmBtu equivalent. On Thursday, September New York city gate gas was pegged at $2.00.
